 The nightmare against Bayern Munich continues for SC Freiburg’s Maximilian Eggestein after 3-1 defeat
 FC Bayern owns Maximilian Eggestein.
 by CSmith1919 Oct 25, 2026, 6:26 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 25 October 2026, Baden-Württemberg, Freiburg im Breisgau: Soccer, Men: Bundesliga, SC Freiburg vs. Bayern Munich, Matchday 7, Europa-Park Stadium. Maximilian Eggestein (left, SC Freiburg) in action against Tom Bischof (FC Bayern Munich). Photo: Harry Langer/dpa (Photo by Harry Langer/picture alliance via Getty Images) Part Of SC Freiburg vs. Bayern Munich: 2026/27 Bundesliga full coverage see all updates CSmith1919 Chuck Smith is the site manager for Bavarian Football Works, where he began writing in 2017. He is the author of The Daily Schmankerl, the longest-running daily Bayern Munich column in English, and also writes The Weekend Warm-Up. In addition to covering Bayern Munich news and providing commentary on Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga, and the German national team. He brings more than 30 years of sports-writing experience to the site. Over the course of his career, he has written for numerous newspapers and websites. With SC Freiburg’s 3-1 defeat to Bayern Munich, SC Freiburg midfielder Maximilian Eggestein has now gone 21 consecutive matches without a victory against the Bavarian giants.
 That is an astonishing run for the SC Freiburg veteran, who has repeatedly found himself on the wrong side of the result whenever he faces Germany’s most successful club. Eggestein transferred to SC Freiburg from Werder Bremen in 2021.
 Bayern Munich once again proved too much to handle, taking all three points and extending Eggestein’s miserable personal record against them. While SC Freiburg has established itself as a difficult opponent for plenty of Bundesliga sides, facing FC Bayern has been an entirely different story for the midfielder.
 Twenty-one matches without a win is not just an unfortunate statistic anymore; it is becoming a rather remarkable streak of bad luck.
 For Bayern Munich, it is another reminder of the psychological edge the club has over so many Bundesliga opponents. For Eggestein, it is another afternoon he would probably rather forget.
 There are difficult opponents, there are bogey teams, and then there is Bayern Munich for Maximilian Eggestein. At this point, he might be wondering what he has to do to finally get one over on the Rekordmeister .
